General.Description:
The Rift appeared on a Tuesday morning and swallowed the city of Orvath whole. By Wednesday, the Conclave of Sorcerers that had maintained the barrier between this world and the void beyond it for six hundred years was gone. The barrier was gone. And the things that lived in the void beyond were beginning, slowly and with evident curiosity, to come through.

Aldric Mourne is the last surviving Conclave sorcerer. He was also the most junior, the least powerful, and the one most recently in disgrace for a violation of Conclave law so minor it would be embarrassing to explain to anyone expecting a grand origin story. What Aldric has that no one else does is a partial understanding of the working that created the Rift — because he was in the archive when the document describing it disappeared, and he has a very good memory.

The Last Sorcerer is an enormously fun and often genuinely thrilling fantasy novel that wears its sense of humour lightly alongside considerable emotional depth. Mira Dawnhallow has built a world that rewards exploration, a magic system of elegant internal consistency, and a protagonist whose self-deprecating narration conceals a moral courage that only becomes visible under pressure.

An outstanding debut. The saga has only just begun.
